decisions.reason: As a close extension of the core cardboard display business, it is likely to stay unless early sales clearly fall below aspirations, and a large firm has enough slack to give such a variant more time.

The pegboard-backed display fits the firm's established capabilities and customer needs, so boundedly rational management would likely retain it while learning about demand rather than stop it quickly.
This quarter-pallet cardboard display sits squarely in the firm's mainstream offer, making it likely to be kept unless results are visibly weak relative to internal and peer aspirations.
Although the eighth-pallet format may be a somewhat narrower niche, it remains close to the firm's proven display portfolio and so would usually be kept during the early market test phase.

The wooden display pallet is somewhat farther from the firm's core cardboard focus and therefore faces a higher risk of failing to meet aspirations, but the firm's scale and solution-oriented model still support keeping it for now.

This media-oriented quarter-pallet display is related to the established business but serves a more specific application, so management would likely continue it unless early performance signals a clear shortfall.
